title: SDK cost-aware slowpath debugging playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook describes a standard, cost-aware approach for diagnosing and resolving SDK-driven slowpaths (high latency or unexpectedly high per-token costs) that impact customer experiences. It is intended for SDK engineers, on-call members, and SREs who handle customer tickets where the observed runtime is slower or more expensive than expected.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: SDK client + runtime interaction, common misconfigurations, and client-side request patterns that amplify server costs. Does not cover low-level GPU kernel bugs (see eng-serving-runtime) or infra supply issues (see eng-sre).
- Goals: Detect slowpath quickly, gather actionable telemetry, reproduce locally, apply low-risk mitigations, and ship a canonical fix or SDK patch.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: SDK platform (eng-developer-experience) — contact channel #sdk-platform.
- Secondary owner: Serving runtime (eng-serving-runtime) — contact #runtime-observability.
- Escalation: If root cause is unclear after 90 minutes of triage, notify on-call SRE via pager and open an incident following the oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process runbook.

Quick summary checklist (fast path):
1) Confirm the customer SLOs and SLAs.
2) Get sample failing request(s) and a flame/trace.
3) Check SDK config: batching, streaming, max_tokens, tokenization mode.
4) Run local repro with the supplied payload and light telemetry capture.
5) Apply mitigation (client-side timeout, prefix cache, fallback model) and monitor.
6) Author canonical fix (SDK or runtime config) and backfill tests.

Diagnostics and thresholds:
- Baseline SLOs (internal reference):
  - median token latency (internal generation path): 20–40 ms/token
  - p95 token latency: <= 150 ms/token
  - request setup time (handshake + routing): <= 50 ms
- Slowpath detection signals:
  - end-to-end request time > 3x expected baseline for similar request sizes
  - sudden token cost increase > 2x historical median for a customer
  - sustained queueing observed in runtime_metrics.queue_depth > 5 for > 60s

Telemetry captures to collect (minimum):
- Client-side:
  - SDK version, adapter, and configuration (batch_size, concurrent_streams, retry_policy)
  - Request headers: X-RW-Debug-ID, X-RW-Trace-Id
  - Tokenized input length and tokenization library/version
- Server-side (ask runtime team or fetch from tracing):
  - Distributed trace (trace_id) with timeline of routing, batching, and kernel exec
  - Per-stage latencies: routing_ms, queue_ms, batch_exec_ms, kv_fetch_ms
  - Model variant and quantization profile used

Telemetry query examples:
- Grafana (Logs/Traces) quick queries:
  - Traces: trace_id="{trace}" | latency > 3000ms | group_by(stage)
  - Metrics: rate(runtime_metrics.queue_depth > 5)[5m] > 1/minute
- Example trace filter (Jaeger-like):
  - search(service=redwood-runtime, tags={trace_id: "{{trace}}"})

Local reproduction quickstart (SDK):
1) Install diagnostic SDK runner (local):
   pip install redwood-sdk-debug==0.6.0  # or npm install @redwood/sdk-debug
2) Capture tokenization output to reproduce exact tokens:
   python -c "from redwood_sdk_debug import TokenDumper; print(TokenDumper.dump(\"<customer prompt>\"))"
3) Run a single-request local replay with 2s of additional client-side logging:
   redwoodctl replay --input sample.json --capture-trace --output trace.json
4) Upload trace.json to internal trace viewer or attach to ticket.

Common root causes and canonical fixes:
1) Over-eager client batching
   - Symptom: large batches cause kernel contention; spikes in batch_exec_ms and queue_ms.
   - Fix: enforce client-side max_batch_bytes and per-tenant batching caps; SDK change: set default max_batch_size=16 for async adapters and provide guidance in README.
   - Example SDK patch (Python):
     client = RedwoodClient(batching={"max_batch_size": 16, "max_batch_bytes": 256000})

2) Misconfigured streaming + retry loops
   - Symptom: duplicate requests, high token counts, elevated cost.
   - Fix: introduce idempotency keys in SDK streaming adapters and stop automatic naive retry for streaming RPCs.
   - Example header: "X-RW-Idempotency-Key: <uuid>"

3) Tokenization variance (different tokenizers between client and runtime)
   - Symptom: request tokens diverge; p50/p95 token count mismatch; billing shows higher tokens.
   - Fix: add deterministic tokenization compatibility mode to SDK; ship token-diff report in repro runner.

4) Frequent small requests without batching (high per-request overhead)
   - Symptom: many tiny requests generating per-request routing and setup costs; p95 route_setup_ms high.
   - Fix: client guidance to use request bundling helper and per-tenant debounce. Provide SDK helper: bundle_or_call().

5) KV cache thrash due to ephemeral conversations
   - Symptom: high kv_fetch_ms and cache miss rate; repeated long prefix walks.
   - Fix: recommend conversation pinning or per-tenant prefix caching policies; runtime can apply soft-ttl to eviction.

Temporary mitigations (low risk) to apply while building canonical fix:
- Enable client-side static model pin fallback to a cheaper variant (e.g., q4_0 -> q8_0) for 5–10 minutes.
- Apply short synthetic rate limit to noisy tenant: rate_limit_override=50r/s.
- Turn on streaming-only mode to reduce per-request setup for streaming workloads.

SDK examples (diagnostic headers and quick toggles):
- Python snippet to attach debug headers:
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
  resp = client.generate(prompt=prompt, headers={"X-RW-Debug-ID": "ticket-1234", "X-RW-Trace-Id": trace_id})
- Node snippet with idempotency key:
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  await client.generate({ prompt, headers: { 'X-RW-Idempotency-Key': uuid() } });

Support triage template (to paste in ticket):
- Customer summary: [brief]
- SDK version and adapter: [sdk, adapter] 
- Sample input (redact PII): [sample prompt]
- Observed latency/cost vs expected: [numbers]
- Attached artifacts: trace.json, token_dump.txt, screenshots
- Assigned owner: @sdk-platform

Docs-site and snippet lifecycle (how to publish an update):
1) Author change in sources/docs-snippets/ with test harness snippet.
2) Add a docs PR against docs-site repo with the snippet ID and QA checklist (snippet must run in the local emulator).
3) Add label "sdk-fix" and the page will be scheduled to the next release train. For emergency patches, contact the docs rotation lead and include the ticket ID.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (recent):
- Issue: sudden cost inflation on transactional chat flows
  - Root cause: client-side synchronous retries calling the generation endpoint on network blips.
  - Canonical fix: SDK v1.14 introduced non-blocking retry policy with jitter and idempotency keys.
- Issue: embedded runtimes seeing 3x latency in mixed embed+generate flows
  - Root cause: requests were not multiplexed and forced sequential kv fetches.
  - Canonical fix: SDK helper bundle_or_call() and runtime batching change release 2025-11.

Postmortem and follow-up steps (after fix):
1) Validate: run golden trace diff on a 72-hour window to ensure no regressions in p95 latency and token costs.
2) Backfill: add an E2E integration test to SDK repo that simulates the customer pattern.
3) Docs: update quickstart sample and add an expandable note in behavior doc explaining the failure mode.
4) Customer comms: share root cause and remediation steps with the customer and note any credits if warranted.

Observability playbook (recommended dashboard panels):
- Panel: SDK version heatmap (per-tenant)
- Panel: Request size vs latency scatter (colored by model_variant)
- Panel: Queue depth and batch_exec_ms over time (stacked)
- Panel: Tokenization mismatch alerts (token_count_client - token_count_server > 20 for > 5 requests)

Automation ideas (backlog):
- Auto-replay agent that runs repros in a sandbox when a support ticket is tagged "auto-repro".
- Preflight validator in the SDK that warns when configurations likely to cause slowpath are used (e.g., max_concurrent_streams > 64 with small batch sizes).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Export a full trace from local runner:
  redwoodctl trace export --trace-id {{trace_id}} --format json > trace.json
- Run a bundle repro locally with token dump:
  redwoodctl replay --input sample.json --tokenize --capture-trace
- Minimal curl example with debug headers:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n    -H "X-RW-Debug-ID: ticket-1234" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd/gpt-1", "prompt":"Hello world", "max_tokens":64}'

References and related pages:
- eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook-2025
- eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-telemetry-collection-2025
- oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Contact and ownership notes:
- For SDK code changes: assign to team "sdk-platform" in Jira (component: sdk-client).
- For runtime investigations: ping #runtime-observability and add the trace_id to the incident.
